core_obligations: Show (2)-(8) are equivalent using intrinsicness of quasi-coherence and the equivalence proposition (proof lines 3778-3786).
Assume (2)-(8) and derive the base-change formula (1) from F(U) = Gamma(U, f^* G) and the pullback compatibility of tilde modules (proof lines 3788-3795).
Assume (1) and prove (2): check the Zariski sheaf condition on a standard cover by rewriting F(U_i) and F(U_i cap U_j) through (1) (proof lines 3797-3815).
Produce, for every U, a presentation of F|_(Aff/S)_Zar/U by free sheaves, by tensoring a presentation of F(U) with the structure sheaf and using right exactness (proof lines 3816-3846).
difficulty_reason: For a presheaf F of O_Aff-modules on (Aff/S)_fppf the lemma gives eight equivalent conditions: the base-change formula F(U') tensor O(U) = F(U) (1), quasi-coherence on the ringed site (Aff/S)_Zar (2) and the same for the etale, smooth, syntomic and fppf topologies (3)-(6), coming from a quasi-coherent module on (Sch/S)_tau for tau in that list via the alternative ringed-site equivalence (7), and coming from a unique quasi-coherent O_S-module by the standard procedure (8) (statement lines 3748-3776). The proof has three parts: intrinsicness of quasi-coherence makes the equivalences (2)-(7) transfer along the alternative equivalence and the equivalence proposition identifies (8) with (7), so (2)-(8) are equivalent; assuming these, the base-change formula (1) is read off from the pullback description F(U) = Gamma(U, f^* G) together with the compatibility of tilde-modules with pullback; and conversely (1) is shown to imply (2) by verifying the Zariski sheaf condition through the cover-module lemma and then producing local presentations by tensoring a presentation of F(U) with the structure sheaf, right exactness of tensor product being the point used (proof lines 3778-3846). The level is H3: three genuinely different arguments, with a displayed presentation-theoretic verification of quasi-coherence at the end.
